summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 1.5/3)

data.turoyo: Ǧəddi saləq lu ṭuro, l Məḏyaḏ. Fayiši bi šawṯo d bə Čalma. Bəṯr šqəlanne, bi šawṯo ʕlayto, bote w maʕmarre w ʕayiši, ǧəddi w babi w ʕammoni ʕam ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: Mein Großvater zog hinauf in den Turabdin, nach Midyat. Sie ließen sich in dem Viertel Bĭ-Čalma nieder. Später kauften sie sich Häuser im Oberen Viertel, sie bauten, und sie lebten (alle) zusammen, mein Großvater, mein Vater und meine Onkel.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive sense-1 cell; explicit family members and co-residence.

summary: All 54 occurrences checked; the homonym ʕyš 2 is not inferred from the English word experience. The new construction belongs to the same I forms as living, not the II observation homonym.

Non-cognate events can be zero-marked objects (Lahdo Traitor 2/82) or fronted and resumed by -le/-e/-te. The experiential subject is indexed by the ordinary personal suffix of Preterit Intransitive; no l-marked experiencer is independently required. The box name remains the glossary's despite transitive event valency.

The specified life in History of Bsorino/9 is cognate and remains I.1, with suffix segmentation uncertain. It is supported by overt ḥaye objects in Hanna Dewo/64 and Interview 2/125; do not split cognate and manner descriptions into separate senses.

Preterit Intransitive can summarize long residence or continuing residence retrospectively; Infectum-wa supplies past living conditions or livelihood. g-/ko- are not mechanically future: heš hul uʕdo gives current continuing experience in Lahdo Traitor 2/82.

Existing examples with omitted sense numbers are assigned to the sole inherited sense 1. Repetitions within a verse have separate decisions but do not become duplicate examples. Existing JL 7.7.4, 20/20, 23/56, 2/122, 4/13, 81/88 and LB 71/Talay 1/71 material is retained.
